sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Real Estate Property Management and Rental Screening Cloud

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement (2012, in force 2013)
Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement between the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits and the Straits Exchange Foundation (ECFA, 2010, effective 2011)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China as revised and effective January 1, 2025; PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3, Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Identification by Market Entities, effective November 1, 2024; Company Law of the People's Republic of China as revised in 2023 and effective July 1, 2024; Regulations on the Administration of Foreign Investment of the People's Republic of China and Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (2024 Negative List); Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration (SAMR, 2021); and, for the Taiwan parent investor, the Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act to the extent consistent with PRC law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan corporate investor (registry extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs / company registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path for non-Hague jurisdictions: (i) extract certified by the Taiwan company registry; (ii) notarized before a Taiwan district court-designated notary public; (iii) verified through the Straits Exchange Foundation; (iv) processed via the ARATS-designated notarization association channel to the receiving PRC notary and local SAMR/AMR; (v) no Hague Apostille is attached; Apostille and Consular Legalization are never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Company Existence of the Taiwan corporate investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs / competent Taiwan company registry, stamped within 90 days before filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path: Taiwan registry issuance, Taiwan notary public notarization, SEF verification, ARATS-side verification through the approved cross-strait notarization channel, then submission to PRC authorities; no Apostille is added because Taiwan is not a Hague Apostille Convention party.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution approving the formation of the China WFOE and appointing the legal representative, together with Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Taiwan corporate investor, notarized by Taiwan notary public and verified through SEF/ARATS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path: sign the board resolution and power of attorney, notarize the signatures before a Taiwan notary public, register the notarized copy with SEF, forward through the ARATS channel to the PRC receiving notary and AMR, and then file with the WFOE formation agent; never append a Hague Apostille to this path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / constitutional documents of the Taiwan corporate investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan company registry as filed, or certified true copy issued by the Taiwan competent registry and notarized by a Taiwan notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path: obtain a registry-certified copy, notarize that copy in Taiwan, verify through SEF, authenticate through the ARATS cross-strait notarization channel, and present the verified copy to PRC notarial and registration authorities; the Hague Apostille procedure is inapplicable and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Taiwan corporate investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank maintaining the corporate investor's account in Taiwan, with bank seal and authorized signatory, then notarized before a Taiwan notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path: issue the bank letter under the bank's letterhead and seal, notarize the authorized signatory's execution, verify the notarization through SEF, transmit through the ARATS channel to the mainland receiving bank and AMR, and use the verified bundle for bank account opening and UBO review; no Apostille is permitted on this path.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be run before any incorporation action against: (i) the revised PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law and PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 beneficial ownership rules; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions Lists; (iii) PRC MPS/PBOC sanctions and red-notice databases; (iv) OFAC SDN List and non-SDN sanctions for USD clearing and any US nexus; (v) EU/UK consolidated financial sanctions for European banking routes; and (vi) Taiwan AML/CFT sanctions and PEP registers applicable to the parent investor. Enhanced due diligence is compulsory for any politically exposed person, family member, or close associate; screening must cover the beneficial owner, legal representative, directors, ultimate parent, controlling shareholders, senior managers, and authorized signatories. Results must be documented, timestamped, and independently reviewed before notarization or SAMR filing; continuous screening and re-screening must occur at least every 90 days and upon any ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Self-Service Registration System, accessed through the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) online government service portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be in Simplified Chinese script; Latin-script, pinyin, or English names may be recorded only as supplementary trade names and cannot replace the legal Chinese name. The statutory four-tier naming structure is: (1) administrative division prefix; (2) distinctive trade name; (3) industry or business-characteristics term; and (4) organization-form suffix such as Limited Liability Company. For a WFOE, the trade name may be a pinyin or Chinese transliteration of the Taiwan parent investor; the name must be distinct after an automated comparison against the national ten-thousand-name database. Traditional Chinese corporate documents from the Taiwan parent must be translated into Simplified Chinese by a licensed translator and notarized; any mismatch between the Chinese legal name and the English translation must be resolved before filing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant receives a written decision stating the statutory grounds. The applicant should immediately file an administrative appeal through the local AMR petition window or the provincial SAMR online appeal module, within the deadline stated in the rejection notice; generally, administrative reconsideration must be filed within 60 days of notice and administrative litigation within 6 months. The appeal must attach the original rejection decision, a revised name plan, a similarity-difference matrix, and supporting priority evidence such as a trademark registration certificate, prior company registration proof, or an explicit consent letter from the prior

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of Taiwan (公司法), 2018 Revision as amended; Articles 18 (company name), 128-129 (incorporation and mandatory Articles of Incorporation contents), 140 (share subscription), 154 (limited liability), 387 (registration filing); combined with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals (外國人投資條例) Articles 7-9 for inbound capital approval; cross-strait document authentication governed by the Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area (兩岸人民關係條例) Article 7.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Administration of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部商業發展署); foreign investment pre-screening conducted by the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部投資審議司), Taipei.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Application Form (公司設立登記申請書) filed through the MOEA One-Stop Online Registration Platform, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation (公司章程), bank capital deposit certificate, consents of first directors, and the Investment Approval Certificate issued by the Investment Commission.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for limited companies in Taiwan after the 2018 Company Act reform; however, the Investment Commission review practice expects a WFOE to remit paid-in capital of at least TWD 1,200,000 (approximately USD 39,000) for operational substance. The full subscribed capital must be remitted from the foreign investor via a designated foreign-exchange bank into a Foreign Investment Capital Deposit Account, and a bank deposit certificate must be issued before incorporation registration. No escrow account is mandated; the deposit certificate suffices under Article 7 of the Company Registration Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the total authorized share capital of the Company is TWD 1,200,000, divided into 1,200,000 ordinary shares of TWD 1.00 par value, fully subscribed by the sole Shareholder, and the paid-in capital is held in the Company's designated deposit account. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be situated at [registered address], Taipei, Taiwan, and the directors are authorized to execute the lease and complete the company registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs. RESOLVED, that [Director A] and [Director B] are appointed as the first directors, and [Officer C] is appointed General Manager, with authority to open bank accounts, execute the incorporation filings, apply for tax and labor registrations, and represent the Company in all statutory registrations until the first annual general meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval by the Investment Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部投資審議司), Taipei; online portal: https://investicc.moea.gov.tw
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Investment by Foreign Nationals (外人投資申請書) through the Investment Commission e-filing system. The Chinese corporate shareholder must file the application with its notarized business registration certificate; documents originating from Mainland China must first be notarized in the Mainland then verified by the Straits Exchange Foundation (海基會) in Taiwan before submission. Attach a concise business plan describing the PropTech SaaS scope, the shareholding ratio, and a capital remittance declaration. The Investment Commission reviews within 10 working days and will issue an Investment Approval Certificate.
required_dossiers: Application for Investment by Foreign Nationals (外人投資申請書)
Mainland notarization and SEF verification certificate for the parent company registration and Power of Attorney
Notarized and SEF-verified Power of Attorney for the Taiwan filing agent
Investment business plan aligned with ISIC 6201 / Taiwan I3010 software services scope
Capital remittance source declaration and bank reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or deferred, the applicant must remedy within 30 days of written notification by submitting supplementary evidence (clarified shareholder chart, revised business plan, or corrected capitalization). An administrative rehearing (訴願) may be filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days after an adverse disposition.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA One-Stop Online Registration Platform (公司與商業及有限合夥一站式線上申請系統), Administration of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online name reservation (公司名稱預查) using the one-stop portal. The proposed Chinese and English names must not be identical with any existing registered entity in the same industry category. Declare the business scope in Chinese using the I3010 software services category (資訊軟體服務業), including 'cloud property management platform, rental screening data analysis, SaaS subscription services', and confirm no restricted industries apply. Pay the NTD 300 name reservation fee.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form with proposed Chinese and English company names
Business scope statement in Chinese corresponding to I3010 and ISIC 6201
No duplicate trademark search declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for duplication, submit up to three alternative names in a single re-filing at no additional fee; if the business scope contains restricted or licensed activities, align the wording with the permitted software services code or obtain the relevant sector license before incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taipei District Court Notary Office or licensed civil notary public in Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation (公司章程) in Chinese, specifying the single corporate shareholder (CN parent), directors (at least one director permitted; this Company uses two), the TWD 1,200,000 paid-in capital, the registered office address in Taipei, and the business object clause referencing software services. Execution by the shareholder's authorized representative must be supported by the SEF-verified Power of Attorney. Notarization is executed before a Taiwan notary public; for mainland-origin signatures, the SEF verification certificate must be annexed.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Chinese
SEF-verified Power of Attorney executed by the CN parent corporate shareholder
Passport copies of authorized directors and signatories
Lease agreement or letter of intent for the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses execution for non-compliant clauses, revise the Articles to conform with Company Act Articles 129-136 and re-submit; a new SEF verification is required if the Power of Attorney must be re-executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Remittance and Bank Deposit Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated Foreign Exchange Bank in Taiwan (e.g., Mega International Commercial Bank, CTBC Bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Investment Approval Certificate, apply to open a Foreign Investment Capital Deposit Account (外資投資資本帳戶) at a Taiwanese bank. Arrange remittance of TWD 1,200,000 from the CN parent. The bank will issue a capital deposit certificate (存款證明) after receipt of funds, which is the statutory evidence of paid-in capital for registration. Do not withdraw or disburse funds until the registration is completed, except for capital verification fees.
required_dossiers: Investment Approval Certificate
Board resolution of the CN parent approving the remittance and capital subscription
Bank account opening forms sealed by the newly appointed directors of the Taiwan WFOE
SEF-verified parent company registration certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the remitted amount deviates more than 10% from the approved capital, file an amendment with the Investment Commission before Continuing Bank verification; if the remittance is blocked by foreign-exchange settlement issues, apply for a supplementary remittance permit through the Central Bank of Taiwan's Foreign Exchange Department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部商業發展署) via One-Stop Online Platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation application through the MOEA one-stop portal. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, bank deposit certificate, consent letters of the two first directors, identification documents of appointees, and the registered office lease. The platform automatically transmits data to the National Taxation Bureau (財政部) for tax registration and to the labor insurance authorities for employer registration, enabling simultaneous issuance of the company registration certificate and tax identification number (統一編號). Pay the registration fee per the Company Registration Fee Standards.
required_dossiers: Company Incorporation Application Form (公司設立登記申請書)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank capital deposit certificate
Consent letters of first directors and supervisor
Identification documents of appointees
Registered office lease agreement with owner consent
Investment Approval Certificate and SEF verification annexes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an order for correction, the company must remedy within 15 days of the written notice; failure to cure results in dismissal of the application, and the petitioner may appeal through administrative petition (訴願). Re-submission fees apply at NTD 1,000 plus NTD 500 per additional corrected item.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Labor, and Commercial Seal Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (財政部各區國稅局), Labor Insurance Bureau (勞動部勞工保險局), National Health Insurance Administration, and local Commerce section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the company automatically receives its tax registration, but must separately: (1) apply for the company seal and responsible person seal engraving; (2) obtain VAT (營業稅) filing credentials and apply for e-invoice (電子發票) eligibility; (3) register as an employer for labor insurance, national health insurance, and labor pension within 8 days of hiring the first employee; (4) notify the local commerce office of the business premises if required for the Taipei municipal fire and sanitation inspection.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Taxpayer Identification Number (統一編號) issuance notice
Company seal and responsible person seal registration cards
Employment contracts and payroll plan
Lease agreement evidence for municipal inspection
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late employer registration is subject to administrative fines under the Labor Insurance Act and National Health Insurance Act; remedy by retroactive registration and payment of arrears, with penalties capped at 10% of unpaid contributions; disputes may be appealed to the Ministry of Labor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board is applicable for the pure cloud SaaS / ISIC 6201 software operation. If the PropTech platform expands into commission-based real estate matching or property management services, the competent authority becomes the Department of Land Administration, Ministry of the Interior (內政部地政司), and a dedicated Real Estate Brokerage License would then be required under the Real Estate Broking Industry Management Act.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required beyond the Company Registration Certificate (公司登記證明書) and the I3010 software-service business scope. No fixed business site permit is required; office occupancy clearance is obtained through the registered office lease and municipal fire safety inspection certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Executive Yuan (環境部)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (免實施環境影響評估) - the company conducts no manufacturing, land development, or stationary emission source operations; only a cloud-based data processing and software platform facility with negligible environmental footprint. No EIA application or registration required under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the core software core function; general compliance applies: office wastewater must connect to the public sewer and meet the Water Pollution Control Act municipal discharge standards; electronic waste (servers, workstations) must be recycled through licensed recyclers in accordance with Article 18 of the Waste Disposal Act; no VOC or stack emissions because there is no manufacturing equipment; cloud servers are hosted by third-party hyperscale providers, so no on-premise data center emissions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: the Taipei City Fire Department requires a fire safety equipment inspection and maintenance report (消防安全設備檢修申報) for the registered office, renewable annually; the landlord must provide an approved fire protection certificate for the commercial building. Structural load inspection: required only if the company installs an on-premise micro data center; not required for standard office use. Occupational clearance: compliance with the Occupational Safety and Health Act Article 6 for office workstation ergonomics, electrical safety, and emergency exit routes; a workplace health risk assessment is recommended prior to employee onboarding.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China (国家税务总局), administered through provincial/municipal tax service bureaus and the national e-Tax portal (https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A PRC WFOE is formed as a resident limited-liability company. The foreign investor first obtains a business license from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), which assigns an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). Tax registration is completed automatically via the multi-license integration system; the WFOE files financing/accounting policy, legal representative, and bank information with the local STA within 30 days. The USCC serves as the statutory tax ID and VAT registration number. For pure foreign vendors without a PRC establishment, the domestic purchaser generally applies reverse-charge or withholding registration; the non-resident supplier may file simplified tax registration through the STA e-platform where China-source services are supplied.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: PRC tax law does not provide a check-the-box election, flow-through election, or hybrid entity election. A WFOE is always a resident enterprise taxable on worldwide income at 25% (15% for qualified high-tech/provided-encouraged industries). A small-scale VAT taxpayer may elect general VAT taxpayer status when annual taxable sales do not exceed RMB 5,000,000; this is a VAT collection method election and does not alter entity-level CIT classification. Hybrid-mismatch adjustments are not elective and are addressed under PRC special tax-adjustment rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for WFOE VAT registration; every enterprise engaged in taxable sales must register for VAT. Annual taxable sales not exceeding RMB 5,000,000 may be classified as a small-scale taxpayer using a simplified 3% levy rate, with possible temporary monthly exemption of RMB 100,000 or quarterly exemption of RMB 300,000. Domestic SaaS/IT services supplied in China by a general VAT taxpayer are normally taxed at 6%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: PRC has implemented fully digital electronic invoices (数电票) through the national electronic invoice platform under the Golden Tax Phase IV system. Invoice data must be transmitted to the STA in near real-time through tax-control integration/APIs. Digital invoices carry a uniform digital signature/cloud stamp; paper invoice systems are being phased out. Export invoices must be electronically matched with customs declarations and foreign-exchange collection records to support zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Caishui [2016] No. 36 Annex 4, PRC VAT zero-rating applies to software services, information system services, R&D services, and other listed cross-border services where: (i) the service recipient is an overseas unit, including a Taiwan-based enterprise treated as outside the mainland customs territory; (ii) the service is wholly consumed outside mainland China; and (iii) the service fee is received in foreign currency and repatriated to the WFOE's PRC bank account. Physical goods exported from mainland China to Taiwan qualify for export VAT zero-rating/rebate where a customs export declaration is completed. Domestic SaaS services supplied to China-resident customers are not zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (出口货物报关单) for physical goods; not required for pure SaaS but required for software/hardware mixed shipments
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export shipment for goods
Inward remittance certificate or bank foreign-exchange collection/settlement certificate (收汇水单) proving repatriation of proceeds
Cross-border service contract or purchase order with the Taiwan-based counterparty and evidence that the service is delivered/consumed outside mainland China
Commercial invoice and packing list for goods; SaaS delivery reports, system logs, or usage records for digital services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export VAT zero-rating and refund claims are subject to strict STA audit. Fraudulent zero-rating, fabricated Taiwan counterparties, circular/repatriated fake export proceeds, forged customs declarations, or false FX certificates result in refund denial and clawback of all rescinded VAT rebates plus interest; administrative fines from 50% to 5 times of evaded tax under the PRC Tax Collection Law; revocation of export rebate qualification; and criminal liability for export-tax-refund fraud under PRC Criminal Law Article 204, with penalties up to life imprisonment for aggravated fraudulent claims. The STA may retrospectively reopen five tax years generally and has no limitation period for collection in cases of fraud or evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) as the central bank and monetary authority, with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) as the delegated regulator of foreign-exchange administration; SAFE operates the bank-led direct registration and current-account declaration system, and national commercial banks licensed by SAFE perform on-the-ground verification of FDI capital accounts, external-debt registrations and profit-remittance checks. Banking supervision of the account-opening institutions is exercised by the National Administration of Financial Regulation (NAFR). Cross-border RMB clearing is supported by the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) operated by the PBOC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Renminbi is freely convertible on the current account for genuine trade in services and software, including the recurring SaaS subscriptions, software licenses, hosting fees and real-estate rental-screening data services contemplated under ISIC code 6201; the bank must verify the underlying contract and invoice, and the enterprise reports each receipt through SAFE's banking information system. Profit remittance (dividends) from the WFOE to its Taiwan shareholder is treated as current-account investment income: it is remittable without SAFE pre-approval, but the remitting bank requires the audited Chinese statutory annual financial statements, the corporate income tax final settlement record showing taxes fully paid, a board or shareholders' resolution declaring the distributable profit, the FDI registration certificate, and, for treaty-reduced withholding, a Taiwan tax residence certificate. Capital-account items are not freely convertible: foreign equity injection above registered capital, cross-border shareholder loans (external debt), outbound investment and offshore listing require SAFE registration or, in some cases, NDRC and MOFCOM approval. The volume and velocity of cross-strait flows must be consistent with China's real-demand FX principle; capital-account RMB converted from the FDI capital account may only be used for the enterprise's genuine operations and cannot be used for equity investment, entrusted loans, wealth-management products or real-property investment. The New Taiwan Dollar (TWD) is not an onshore deliverable currency; cross-strait trade and service payments are commonly invoiced and remitted in USD or CNH with TWD converted by the Taiwan-side bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The PRC statutory surrender and mandatory conversion-ratio system for export proceeds has been abolished; an exporter may keep any portion of its foreign-currency export receipts in a foreign-currency current account at a domestic designated bank or convert to RMB at the bank's daily quotation. For goods exports, the enforceable discipline is the collection requirement: export proceeds must be repatriated into a PRC bank account and collected within 180 days of the customs export declaration date; overdue collections must be reported to the bank and SAFE. For service exports, which cover the WFOE's SaaS and PropTech contracting, there is no fixed time-to-conversion and no mandatory conversion ratio; the proceeds may remain in a foreign-currency account, but the receipt must be reported truthfully to SAFE through the settlement bank under the service-trade and other-current-items reporting regime using the correct purpose code (for example, software-related services) and the supporting service contract must be retained for at least five years. The same treatment applies to receipts aggregated by licensed cross-border payment institutions under a centralized collection product, where the PSP and the domestic bank jointly verify the aggregated export claims.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of China Limited - Corporate Banking and International Settlement Department
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI capital account plus multi-currency operational current account
RMB basic and general operating account, foreign-currency current account, and cross-border digital collection portal

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB settlement account and SAFE-registered FX capital and foreign-currency operating accounts
Dual-currency RMB and foreign-currency corporate account with a regional network for Taiwan and ASEAN settlement
FX settlement account and capital-account administration for foreign-invested enterprises

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for merchant collection and low-value subscription rails; Low for primary banking and treasury escrow. Offshore digital EMIs (Airwallex, Currenxies, WorldFirst, Revolut Business, Mercury and similar) cannot lawfully act as the primary relationship bank or SAFE-verified settlement bank for a PRC-incorporated WFOE; the WFOE's receipts must be repatriated to a domestic designated bank's foreign-currency account or through a PBOC-licensed cross-border payment institution with centralized collection. The permissible architecture: the offshore EMI or PSP collects Stripe Billing and ACH Direct proceeds, aggregates net settlement, and executes a single or batched SWIFT wire to the WFOE's domestic foreign-currency account; the domestic bank captures the aggregated receipts under service-trade reporting with the PSP's settlement statement as the supporting voucher. The legal constraints are that EMIs are payment-service enterprises rather than banks in China; they cannot open deposit accounts, cannot receive FDI capital injections or external-debt drawdowns, cannot provide onshore FX derivatives, and cannot be used for the reinvestment or distribution of capital-account funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is mandatory in substance. Under PBOC and NAFR corporate-account rules and standard bank policy, the WFOE's legal representative (or a written delegate holding a notarized power of attorney issued in Chinese and confirmed by the board) must appear in person at the relevant bank branch for the initial face-to-face KYC interview, and the bank will conduct an on-site verification of the registered business address and confirm the company seal, financial seal, tax invoice seal and legal representative's signature card. Remote or video-only onboarding is not available for a newly formed Taiwan-owned WFOE with cross-border needs; the complete opening sequence is: (1) online submission of scanned corporate documents and pre-screening by the account manager; (2) physical interview and seal confirmation at the branch; (3) bank site inspection; (4) final authorization signature by the legal representative or power-of-attorney holder; and (5) activation of the RMB and FX accounts after the bank verifies the business license and SAFE FDI registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by a Taiwan shareholder holding via an offshore BVI or Hong Kong intermediate layer and a newly registered mainland WFOE with no prior banking history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate ownership chart from ultimate beneficial owners to the WFOE; certified Taiwan company registration, registry extracts for BVI or Hong Kong interposed entities; PBOC-compliant ultimate-beneficial-owner declaration form; passport copies, residence permits and source-of-wealth statements for all individuals owning 25 percent or more; notarized power of attorney; original business license and company seal card; reference letter from a home-country or Taiwan bank where available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value cross-border subscription receipts from Taiwan clients via Stripe Billing and ACH Direct, which are aggregated by a US payment service provider and do not match the typical goods-export pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed SaaS subscription and software-license agreements with pricing and jurisdiction clauses; itemized invoices and monthly statements; PSP merchant agreement, payment-route configuration, settlement reports and transaction-reconciliation files mapping each batch to underlying invoices; product website, API and SDK documentation and cloud service contracts proving the service is performed; customer KYB files for material accounts; refund and dispute policy; documentation of the bank's centralized service-trade declaration entries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Misalignment between the registered business scope (ISIC 6201, no statutory license) and the declared payment rails and overseas client base, which may trigger a shell-entity underwriter flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business license with matching scope; local office lease and utility contracts; payroll and social-insurance records for employees in mainland China; corporate website and product demonstration environment; domestic and Taiwan customer contracts; contracts with cloud providers, data centers and hosting vendors; evidence of recurring-revenue recognition under PRC accounting standards; five-year document-retention policy; statement that no negative-list activities such as real-estate brokerage or financial services are carried out.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dividend remittance to the Taiwan shareholder occurring in the early years of operation, when accumulated profits and tax history are short, raising withholding-tax and profit-authenticity concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full-audit Chinese statutory financial statements; corporate income tax annual settlement schedules and tax-payment receipts; board or shareholders' resolution on profit distribution; withholding-tax computation (10 percent statutory rate, 5 percent only where the Taiwan shareholder is the beneficial owner holding the required tax-residence certificate); SAFE FDI registration certificate; written confirmation of no outstanding tax or customs liabilities; bank references covering the source of funds used to capitalize the WFOE.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically-exposed-person and adverse-media hits on ultimate owners, particularly where a China-Taiwan dual connection or a US or EU nexus creates an enhanced-scrutiny profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and PEP screening output from a licensed data provider covering UN, OFAC, EU and PRC lists; beneficial-owner attestation and passport copies; media search report; board resolution authorizing the banking relationship and stating a clean source-of-wealth position; independent legal counsel opinion on ultimate-beneficial-owner analysis under PRC AML rules; commitment to provide ongoing transaction monitoring and to notify the bank of any change in ownership.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant routing for the Taiwan shareholder's capital contribution is a SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own account at a Taiwanese bank to the WFOE's SAFE-designated FDI capital account at the selected domestic bank. Preconditions: completion of foreign-invested enterprise registration, SAFE direct-investment registration through the receiving bank or its digital foreign-exchange system, and completion of the bank's KYC file. The remitter must be the registered shareholder itself; third-party remittances are prohibited. Upon receipt, the bank credits the USD or CNH to the capital account and, under the payment-based conversion and use-based settlement regime, the WFOE may convert the proceeds to RMB and place them in a capital-use RMB account, then make disbursements against genuine vouchers of business use (salaries, rent, hosting, software subcontracting and marketing); surplus funds stay in the foreign-currency or RMB capital account only while awaiting genuine payment obligations. Any use beyond ordinary operations, such as an intra-group loan to another PRC entity or an equity investment, requires separate SAFE approval. An alternative parent-funding rail is an external-debt shareholder loan from the Taiwan parent: before the first drawdown the loan must be registered through the bank under the macro-prudential external-debt regulation, with the principal within the statutory borrowing ceiling calculated by reference to the WFOE's net assets and the regulatory leverage factor; funds are remitted by MT103, converted under the same use-based discipline, and repaid with interest after the loan has been closed at SAFE; debt-service payments require the pre-registered repayment plan and the bank's verification of interest invoices.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The WFOE's outbound clearing architecture should combine four rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for deterministic one-off payments covering cloud-hosting invoices, Taiwan and global software subcontractors, legal and financial advisers, overseas marketing and eventual dividends; each payment is verified against the supporting contract or invoice and reported by the bank to SAFE as an outward current-account payment; (2) CIPS for RMB-denominated settlements to Taiwanese and regional counterparties, avoiding USD correspondent-chain friction; (3) commercial letters of credit (MT700 and MT707) only where physical goods such as sensor hardware or integrated PropTech devices accompany the service contract, and therefore not a principal liquidity tool; and (4) the Stripe Billing and ACH Direct collection rail, aggregating low-value subscription income through the PSP and repatriating net proceeds to the domestic settlement account under a centralized collection arrangement, with each batch mapped to the SAFE service-trade declaration. For dividend or royalty payments to the Taiwan shareholder, the bank requires the audited financial statements, corporate income tax final-settlement receipts, board resolution, SAFE FDI registration evidence, the non-resident withholding-tax payment certificate, and a tax-residence certificate where a treaty-reduced or cross-strait-reduced withholding rate is applied; the remittance is then executed by MT103 in USD or CNH with the outward-remittance voucher reported through the SAFE system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB forwards executed with a SAFE-licensed domestic bank on a real-demand basis, matched to forecasted USD or CNH current-account receipts and payments
Foreign-exchange swaps between RMB and USD or CNH for short-dated treasury liquidity alignment
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for long-tenor external-debt or vendor-financing exposures, subject to the bank's eligibility review and real-demand verification

Plain-vanilla FX options and option combinations (puts, calls, collars and risk reversals) with the settlement bank, used exclusively to hedge identifiable underlying current-account or registered capital-account exposure; offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards may not be overlaid because they are inconsistent with SAFE's real-demand discipline and would create an unattested FX position

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Registration and Beneficial-Owner Declaration (公司年度申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Law – One-Stop Online Company Registration System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June each year (within six months after fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission or non-submission may incur a fine of NT$10,000– NT$50,000 (approx. US$320–US$1,600); continued default may trigger compulsory dissolution and administrative strike-off by MOEA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign-Invested Operation Report and Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after fiscal year-end (normally by 28/29 February for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in fines under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, suspension of profit and capital repatriation privileges, and potential revocation of the foreign-investment approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Financial Statements (營利事業所得稅結算申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (regional office, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the following year (within five months after fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and underpayment attract a monthly penalty of 3% of unpaid tax, up to a cap of 30%, plus interest on arrears; prolonged non-filing can lead to tax assessment and referral to MOEA for corporate strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit by a licensed Taiwan CPA is triggered when (i) paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million (approx. US$1.0 million), (ii) annual operating revenue exceeds NT$50 million (approx. US$1.6 million), (iii) the company engaged in banking, insurance, securities, or other FSC-regulated activities, or (iv) the Investment Commission imposes an audit requirement as a condition of foreign-investment approval.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private companies apply Taiwan Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (T-GAAP) under the Business Accounting Act (商業會計法); companies meeting certain size thresholds may elect to adopt International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as endorsed by Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Article 22-1 of the Taiwan Company Act, every company must annually confirm and file its substantial controllers / beneficial-owner information through the MOEA One-Stop Online Registration System as part of the June annual declaration; any change occurring during the year must be separately reported within 15 days of such change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$200 – US$800 per year (Taiwan corporate service provider registered office / agent service)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,000 – US$5,000 per year (Taiwan CPA firm audit fee, if the audit threshold is met)
